2. **Lack of Jurisdiction**: Where there is a clear violation of principles of natural justice in that the learned judge failed to disclose his connection with the subject-matter or parties, giving scope for an apprehension of bias.

The judgment also specifies that such curative petitions should be first circulated to a Bench of three senior-most Judges and those who passed the order. The Bench must conclude that the matter needs hearing before it is listed before the same Bench (as far as possible) which may pass appropriate orders.

In Mohd. Arif @ Ashfaq vs The Reg. Supreme Court Of India & Ors (2014), while discussing a curative petition, this Court reiterated its stance on limited oral hearings for cases in this class of situations to ensure justice is served efficiently and fairly.

Therefore, the circumstances under which the Supreme Court can entertain a curative petition are when there has been a violation of principles of natural justice or where there was a lack of jurisdiction.
